decisions.quote: In this study we replicate the extended BXS [19] cross-nationally to measure differences in the ways consumers experience the eco-friendliness of global smartphone brands in a cross-national context. The survey items were selected from the previously developed and extended BXS [18,19,107]. We assess the four items measuring eco-friendliness as well as the other four brand experience dimensions from the BXS by conducting structural equation modeling (SEM) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) following the same steps that Brakus et al. [18] undertook.
decisions.reason: The paper collects survey data from Finland (N = 506) and India (N = 502) to empirically re-test the factor structure and validity of the Brand Experience Scale (BXS) of Brakus et al. (2009) [18] and its eco-friendliness extension by Saari (2016) [19].

decisions.quote: We have replicated and tested cross-nationally an existing BXS [18] that has been extended with an eco-friendliness subscale [19] and measured how consumers in India and Finland experienced the eco-friendliness of three major smartphone brands.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row (10.1509/jmkg.73.3.052) and blind target 0 (10.1509/jmkg.73.3.52) identify the same re-tested original paper, Brakus, Schmitt, and Zarantonello (2009) [18], differing only in a leading zero in the page segment of the DOI.

decisions.quote: However, based on our study the dimensions for eco-friendly, sensory, affective, and behavioral brand experiences are generalizable cross-nationally in India and Finland. Even so, our findings suggest that the intellectual aspects of the brand experience should be localized with special expertise of the consumer groups in the target country.
decisions.reason: When testing the four original BXS dimensions of Brakus et al. (2009) [18], the sensory, affective, and behavioral dimensions were supported in both countries, whereas the intellectual dimension and negatively worded items failed to meet factor loading and fit thresholds in India and had to be excluded from the revised model.
